glosses: royal
Royal, royale.

examples.text: Damit wird jede weitere Kritik an der Handhabe der Krise für Thailänder heikel: Diese könnte nach dem royalen Statement als Beleidigung des Königs ausgelegt werden, worauf bis zu 15 Jahre Gefängnisstrafe stehen.

glosses: den König/die Königin, das Königshaus betreffend, zu ihm/ihr gehörend

examples.text: Die royale Familie macht wieder einmal Schlagzeilen.

glosses: den König/die Königin oder die Monarchie als Staatsform unterstützend

examples.text: „Das Ziel einer Stärkung der royalen Kräfte nahm der bisherige Premierministers Marouf Al Bakhit bereits am Wahltag in einer Fernsehansprache vorweg […]“.

translations.source_sense_description: den König/die Königin, das Königshaus betreffend, zu ihm/ihr gehörend

glosses: Of or relating to a monarch or his (or her) family.

examples.text: He tried to persuade Cicely to stay away from the ball-room for a fourth dance. […] But she said she must go back, and when they joined the crowd again her partner was haled off with a frightened look to the royal circle, […]
On the first Friday morning of his kingship he went into the kitchen and called for his royal chef.

glosses: Having the air or demeanour of a monarch; illustrious; magnanimous; of more than common size or excellence.

examples.text: How doth that royal Merchant good Anthonio;

glosses: In large sailing ships, of a mast right above the topgallant mast and its sails.

examples.text: royal mast;  royal sail

glosses: Free-for-all, especially involving multiple combatants.
Used as an intensifier.

examples.text: a royal pain in the neck

glosses: Describing a piece which, if captured, results in loss of game.

examples.text: Maharajah and the Sepoys pits a single royal amazon for white against a standard chess army for black.

glosses: A royal person; a member of a royal family.

examples.text: Andy noted in RAIL 462: "The Royals are bound to have a great say in the decoration of the train and it speaks volumes for their regard for it that there are so many portraits of previous Royal Trains and items presented on trips. I sense they're extremely fond of it."

glosses: A standard size of printing paper, measuring 25 by 20 inches.
A standard size of writing paper, measuring 24 by 19 inches.
The Australian decimal currency intended to replace the pound in 1966; was changed to \"dollar\" before it was actually circulated.
Any of various lycaenid butterflies.
The fourth tine of an antler's beam.
A stag with twelve points (six on each antler).
In large sailing ships, square sail over the topgallant sail.

examples.text: in ten days after we spoke the Solon, so rapid was his recovery, that, from lying helpless and almost hopeless in his berth, he was at the mast-heId, furling a royal.

glosses: An old English gold coin, the rial.
A small mortar.
In auction bridge, a royal spade.
A tuft of beard on the lower lip.
Bell changes rung on ten bells.
